blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — How much consumers pay for seafood in the Caraga region depends heavily on whether they live by the sea or deep inland, regional market data showed. A price monitoring report by the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (DA-BFAR) Caraga revealed a stark economic divide during the second week of October: coastal towns enjoyed cheaper marine catches, while landlocked communities paid steep premiums to cover long-haul logistics and cold storage.
